newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Oct 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Oct 31.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Vlakplaas murder squad commander Eugene de Kock had to spend the rest of his life behind bars to pay for his heinous crimes "condoned and covered up by a system rotten to the core", the Transvaal Supreme Court ruled.
- Swiss bank UBS predicted that the rand would stabilise over the coming months and that it would appreciate relative to inflation differentials next year.
- Chemicals manufacturer Sentrachem boosted earnings 17 percent to 249 million rand for the year to August.
- Coronation Holdings and Trencor have formed Trencoro, a financial services company capitalised at 200 million rand.

- The governments of Mozambique and Zimbabwe, along with JCI and U.S. energy company Arco, are embarking on the first stage of a 2.8-3.0 billion rand iron ore project in the Beira corridor using natural gas from the Temane field in Mozambique.
- Chemicals manufacturer Sentrachem lifted earnings before exceptionals 6.3 percent to 131.2 cents a share in the year to August 31.
- Mark Barnes, deputy managing director at Standard Corporate and Merchant Bank, will leave the bank to become chief executive of the Capital Alliance Financial Services group.
- The rand broke through the 4.74 level against the dollar, continuing its string of record lows.
- Apartheid killer Eugene de Kock will stay in jail even if his amnesty application to the Truth and Reconciliation Commission is successful.

- South African Defence Force operatives murdered activist Fabian Ribeiro and his wife Florence in 1986, and top military and police were behind the cover-up, the truth commission's amnesty committee heard.
